subject: Business Models
title: Supply Chain Control
description: A 60-second lesson on Supply Chain Control.

hook.text: McDonald's requires franchisees to buy supplies from approved vendors. The fries, buns, and cups are all mandated.

buildup.text: Mandatory suppliers ensure consistency. A Big Mac tastes the same in Tokyo, Paris, and rural Ohio.

discovery.text: Franchisors negotiate bulk pricing centrally, often passing savings to franchisees—but not always.

twist.text: Some franchisors earn kickbacks from mandatory suppliers. They profit from both royalties and supply chain markups.

climax.text: Supply chain control is both a quality tool and a profit center. The line between them is blurry.

punchline.text: Mandatory suppliers: quality control or profit grab? Often both.

quiz.question: Why do franchisors mandate specific suppliers?
options: Consistency and sometimes franchisor profit from kickbacks

details.summary: Franchisors often require franchisees to purchase supplies exclusively from approved vendors or the franchisor's own supply company. This control ensures product consistency across locations but also generates significant profit for the franchisor through supply chain markups and volume rebates.
details.whyItMatters: Supply chain control is a hidden profit center in franchising. Franchisors may earn as much from supply markups as from royalties. Understanding this reveals the true cost of franchise ownership beyond the headline fee percentages.
takeaways: Franchisors mandate approved vendors to maintain product consistency system-wide
Supply chain markups and rebates generate significant franchisor revenue
Franchisees may pay above-market prices for required proprietary supplies

faq.question: How do franchisors profit from supply chain control?
faq.answer: They negotiate volume discounts from suppliers and pass only partial savings to franchisees. They earn rebates on franchisee purchases that are not disclosed. Some operate proprietary supply companies with profit margins built into pricing..

faq.question: Can franchisees negotiate or find alternative suppliers?
faq.answer: Typically no. Franchise agreements mandate specific suppliers or the franchisor's own supply company. Franchisees who source independently risk termination for contract violation. Some franchise associations have successfully negotiated better supply terms collectively.
